# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm first to observe but Mute goes before me in turn order, and Blind goes after me. Since I can't hear speech, I don't know what Mute has told Blind yet. I should share what I see, directed appropriately since Blind can't see gestures and Mute can't hear... wait, I can speak to both Mute and Blind (they can hear me), but only Mute receives my gestures too (Blind can't see).

Let me report the bomb's display clearly via speech so Blind (who can hear) and Mute (who can hear) both get it. This establishes shared info before Mute's manual knowledge can be matched to it next round.

```
speak(text="Display shows the number 8. Light is green. There are three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute gestured ☝ to me — a single raised finger. Since I can't hear speech, this gesture is the only info I get this round. It might mean "wire 1" or "one thing at a time" or "wait" — ambiguous, but likely pointing to wire 1 given the board layout. I don't have enough to act since I can't touch anything anyway. I should acknowledge and pass along that I saw the gesture, and repeat the bomb state in case Blind still needs it (Blind hears speech).

Let me speak to Blind (and Mute, since Mute hears too) confirming what I see, in case Mute is trying to confirm details before instructing Blind next turn.

```
speak(text="Confirming again: display 8, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. I saw a single gesture from Mute, looked like one raised finger, possibly indicating wire 1.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute is repeating the same gesture ☝ to me again. This is likely confirming "wire 1" as significant — perhaps the manual says to cut wire 1, or asks about wire 1 specifically, and Mute wants me to confirm something about wire 1 by sight (like its color) since Mute can't see the bomb.

Since I already told them wire 1 is red, this repeated ☝ might be Mute acknowledging/confirming that wire 1 is the one in question, or Mute might be waiting for me to react differently. I should confirm wire 1's color specifically and clearly, in case my earlier full report wasn't parsed as directly answering "what is wire 1".

```
speak(text="Wire 1 is red. Repeating: display 8, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 👆]

Blind is gesturing to me now — but wait, Blind cannot see gestures! Let me reconsider: the rules say Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." So Blind shouldn't be able to send *meaningful* gestures to me either... but actually, the rules about gesture-sending don't restrict who can gesture, only who can perceive them. Blind can still physically gesture (make hand motions), even if blind - that's a physical action, not sight-dependent. And I can see gestures since I'm Deaf (not blind).

So Blind sent me 🙏 (pray/please) and 👆 (point up). This might be Blind asking for help, or asking about something above/first. Given wire 1 was highlighted by Mute, and now Blind is asking "please, point up / first one" — likely Blind wants confirmation about wire 1, or is asking me to confirm which wire to cut.

I should respond with speech since Blind can hear me.

```
speak(text="Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. Display shows 8, light is green. If you are asking about the first wire, it is red.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new arrivals this round — meaning Mute didn't gesture to me, and I don't hear Blind's speech anyway. Let me just keep reinforcing the board state so it's always fresh for both listeners, since I don't know what's landed for them or what stage they're at with the manual.

```
speak(text="Still confirming board: display 8, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute keeps sending ☝ (single raised finger) to me repeatedly. This is a consistent, deliberate signal — likely confirming "wire 1" is correct/relevant per the manual, or asking me a yes/no confirmation using a single gesture meaning "one" or "first."

Since gestures are the only channel Mute has to me, and this is the third time receiving the identical single symbol, it's likely Mute wants me to confirm "wire 1" as the target, and is waiting for my acknowledgment. Since I can't gesture confirmation understanding back in a way Mute would parse differently, I should use speech to explicitly confirm wire 1 is red and ask Blind to act on cutting wire 1, since Blind can hear my speech.

Given the persistent signal and no contradicting info, I'll commit to instructing based on this: wire 1 (red) seems to be the one indicated.

```
speak(text="Instruction for Blind: cut wire 1, the red wire. Confirming board again: display 8, light green, wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
wait()
```
